made: node docs/proyecto/pixel/tiendas-sheet-make.js, from tiendas-set.html (window.TIENDAS.E) and the design of Las tiendas (the orchestrator's p5-spec, section tiendas). A new scene: no old scene, no remap.

rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin: sx = OX + (x - y) / R2 * S, sy = OY + ((x + y) / R2 * .5 - z * COS) * S, depth d = (x + y) / R2 * COS + z * .5 (R2 = sqrt 2, COS = sqrt 3 / 2); OX = W / 2 + originX, OY = H / 2 + originY. A box is the screen bounding box of its 8 projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)]. screen is the projection rounded to whole pixels. The row's wall is y = 0 (the fronts face +y); the pavement runs from it to y = 2.6, the kerb to y = 2.8, then the street. This is the state fila = tiendas; fila = altos has its own origin, spots and view in `altos`
rules.spot: a spot is a world point of the feet (z 0: the pavement; z 0.46: the seat's top; z 0.72: the horse's back; z 0.9: the handlebar of Luis's bicycle) and, drawn there, a character stands with its feet (the lowest row the sprite draws, outline included) resting on the screen row sy, i.e. the sprite's bottom edge on sy, and its middle column on the column sx (rules.anchor). scale is the frog's: 1 everywhere. spot.sprite says which maker stands there in the preview (the make's checks use it); the game may put someone else there
rules.anchor: the column of the sprite that is on sx; its feet (its lowest drawn row, outline included) rest on row sy - 1, so its bottom edge is on sy. mkPersona (48 wide): column 24 (KIT.PX), 53 rows drawn standing (a 56-row canvas whose lowest row is empty), a child 41 rows; the frog mkCoqui(1) (32 x 27): column 16, drawn rows 1 to 24 (so row 25 of the canvas is on sy, as juego.js frogBox: his shadow line q.y + 25); abuela standing mkAbuela (48 x 51): column 30, drawn rows 0 to 49; abuela sitting mkAbuelaS (52 x 50): column 17 (her middle) and row 36 (her lap) on (sx, sy), the spot being the seat; Luis sitting mkPersona(..., sent = 1): feet on sy; the stroller with the bebé (a stand-in, 26 x 36): column 13, its wheels' bottom on sy; Luis's bicycle (a stand-in, 44 x 34): the handlebar's column 28 on sx; a small thing: its bottom middle on the point. Widths of the boxes for the checks: the frog 32, a grown-up 24, a child 24, the stroller 26 (its stand-in's own width: the spec gives none)
rules.view: a view has a zoom (here 1: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture) and x0, kept inside 0 .. 44. Never a fraction
rules.depth: a spot's depth is the engine's d of its world point (z counts: d = (x + y) / R2 * COS + z * .5); front.plane turns it into the depth of each row of a character. The frog on the handlebar stands in the same upright plane as Luis (same x, y): the two tie, and the frog is drawn after him
rules.doors: a front is the lit wall x0 .. x1 (E.FW wide), y = 0, h high (E.H, the banco .25 more); its door from x0 + E.DOOR, E.DW wide, E.DH high, with a frame .12 wider on each side and .12 higher; its sign (a board on the wall, y .03) .22 in from each side, from E.DH + .18 to h - .06. fronts[] below lists the numbers the checks use

front.how: no list. A character is hidden by every set pixel that is nearer the camera than the character's feet (depth test against the baked depth, with the feet's depth plus 0.3), so a front hides nobody who stands in front of it, the seat's back hides nobody who sits on it, and a person at a door is whole.
front.plane: for the character's pixel on picture row r (r = 0 at the top): depth(r) = d + (sy - (r + .5)) * tan(30 deg) / S, where d is the spot's depth and sy its screen row; the pixel is hidden where bakedZ[r * 240 + x] > depth(r) + bias (bakedZ: window.DEPTH.z of the set page). The upright plane through the feet, as El mostrador's front; the same test for people, the stroller and the small things
front.sprites: between two sprites the nearer pixel wins: the same depth(r), no bias; equal depths: the one drawn later (the frog on the handlebar is drawn after Luis)
